newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia hopes for reduction in external debt.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia hopes for reduction in external debt.

text.p: Ethiopia hopes a conference of world financial institutions in Washington in October will write off up to 90 percent of the $3 billion external debt it has been burdened with since the late Emperor Haile Selassie.

Finance Minister Sufian Ahmed told state-run Ethiopian News Agency on Wednesday that Ethiopia was one of the nations whose debt reduction would be discussed at the Washington meeting sponsored by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"We hope creditor financial institutions will make a substantial reduction in the accumulated $3 billion debt so we can forge ahead with the development of the country," he said.
Sufian said Ethiopia annually committed up to 47 percent of its export earnings to service its huge external debt.
He expressed gratitude for a $1.2 billion donation by Western nations in 1992 to repair the damage of 17 years of Marxist rule.
In 1992, Ethiopia embarked on an ambitious programme to revive an economy suffering from the policies of exiled dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam, famine and civil war.
It devalued the birr currency by 58.6 percent, liberalised prices and encouraged private enterprise which had virtually vanished.
